blindSummary:
This country under its current regime is the most hostile environment surveyed here for a transgender person. The 2024 morality code obliges the regime's virtue police to prevent "homosexuality" and "lesbianism"; the regime applies the death penalty for same-sex relations under its interpretation of religious law; and documented practice against LGBTIQ people includes beatings, sexual violence in detention, forced confessions, and house-to-house searches. Transgender people in the country report living in hiding, in windowless rooms, for years.

There is no legal recognition, no protection, no functioning consular protection, and no tourism infrastructure that would allow a visitor to blend in. A discovered trans visitor would face the same enforcement apparatus as local LGBTIQ people: detention with routine sexual and physical abuse of queer detainees, prosecution for moral crimes, and corporal punishment that UN experts say is escalating into 2026.
blindOutOfScope: Armed conflict, terrorism, kidnapping, and the arbitrary detention of foreign nationals for leverage are severe risks for every visitor to this country, independent of any personal characteristic.
blindSourceSummaries: A regional asylum agency's 2024 country guidance note, section 3.17: assesses LGBTIQ persons as a risk profile for international protection under the current regime in this country.

The same agency's country-of-origin information report, section 4.5: detailed country-of-origin information on the situation of LGBTIQ+ persons, including punishment under the de facto authorities in this country.

International human-rights organisations' joint report (Jan 2022) with a title conveying that nowhere is safe, based on 60 interviews with LGBT people after the regime takeover. Documents regime members attacking or threatening people because of sexual orientation or gender identity, abuse from family members and neighbours who support the regime, people fleeing their homes, and lives built over years disappearing overnight.

International LGBT-rights organisation report (Feb 2023) on 18 months of the regime's persecution of LGBTIQ people, based on interviews with 22 LGBTIQ residents still in the country (Sept-Oct 2022). Finds regime security officials pursuing LGBTIQ people - especially gay men and trans women - more systematically than in the first months of rule, with physical and sexual assault, arbitrary detention, and public flogging for alleged same-sex relations confirmed by the regime's top court on social media.

Foreign public broadcaster (Oct 2021): profile of a trans man hiding in a windowless back room in the capital after the takeover, and his gay friend. Describes LGBTQ people facing the death penalty under regime rule and the only realistic option being to flee the country.

Legal news feature (Nov 2024) on findings by an LGBTQ+ refugee self-organisation from this country operating in the diaspora. Documents systematic persecution under regime rule; notes that even before 2021 no legal framework protected LGBTQ people, and that transgender individuals are especially exposed.

Translation of the enforcement article of the regime's 2024 morality law (a 'promotion of virtue and prevention of vice' code) by a transitional-justice project. The article tasks morality enforcers with preventing a wide range of 'evils' including adultery and related conduct, codifying moral surveillance that reaches LGBTQ+ identity, women's public speech, and cultural expression.

A UN human-rights experts' statement (Mar 2026): condemns this regime's surging judicially sanctioned public floggings — at least 1,110 people in 2025 alone, nearly double the prior year — warning women, girls and LGBT+ people face heightened punishment for so-called 'moral crimes' including 'illicit relationships' and 'sodomy'.
Rights-group country profile: this country criminalises same-sex sexual activity between men and between women, with severe penalties. (Only the opening of the profile was retrievable at fetch time.)
A cable-news report (Nov 2024): LGBTQ people in this country describe arbitrary detention, beatings and abuse in custody as the ruling regime's crackdown intensifies.
